Proposal No: UPGI-26-PR100

Consultancy Type: Short Term

Publication Date: 16/11/2026

Consultants Location: Philippines

Organisational Background

BRAC was established after the independence of Bangladesh by Sir Fazle Hasan Abed in 1972 and is currently working in 10 other countries in Asia and Africa. It is the largest non-governmental development organisation in the world in terms of number of employees. BRAC International is a leading nonprofit organisation with a mission to empower people and communities in situations of poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our approach is to identify innovative and holistic solutions toward sustainable livelihoods and socioeconomic resilience. We achieve large-scale, transformative change by empowering individuals, especially women, and their families and communities to overcome poverty and become self-reliant and resilient. We work with local communities to innovate demand-driven programmes that integrate social development with market-based solutions like microfinance and social entrepreneurship. With our origin and roots in the Global South and our commitment to continuous learning, we have a depth of experience and evidence that enables us to respond to the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage.

About the BRAC International’s Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative (BI-UPGI)

BRAC’s Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative (UPGI) is a global unit of BRAC that was founded in 2016 to build off the success of BRAC’s Ultra-Poor Graduation program in Bangladesh. BRAC UPGI aims to position the Graduation approach as a key driver to eradicate extreme poverty worldwide. It does this by:

  • Advocating for uptake of the Graduation approach by policymakers, national governments, multilateral institutions, and non-governmental organizations; and

  • Effective adaptation and implementation of the Graduation approach in countries around the world, supported through technical assistance and capacity strengthening for external stakeholders.

In 2002, BRAC pioneered the Ultra-Poor Graduation (“Graduation”) approach in Bangladesh - a holistic intervention to help people lift themselves from extreme poverty - after recognizing that existing poverty alleviation programs were not reaching the poorest people. Through the provision of livelihood assets, cash transfers, and continued mentoring and training, the Graduation approach addresses participants’ multidimensional needs within the local context and ‘graduates’ people from extreme poverty into sustainable livelihoods.

Graduation is an evidence-based, scalable intervention proven to break the poverty trap for the long term. So far, BRAC’s flagship Graduation program has impacted over 2 million Bangladeshi households—totaling over 9 million people. To help eradicate extreme poverty, BRAC UPGI is working to scale globally by integrating Graduation into existing government programs and help 21 million more people lift themselves from extreme poverty by 2026.

But BRAC UPGI cannot do it alone. This is beyond the means and capacity of a single organization- no matter how ambitious or innovative. Sustainability and scale demand change at the systems level with active government engagement. BRAC UPGI is committed to creating effective solutions that leverage the available resources and existing programming to achieve the long-term benefits demonstrated by Graduation. The organization is partnering with governments, as well as multilateral institutions, NGOs, and civil society, in countries where BRAC UPGI thinks it can have maximum impact and drive greater uptake for Graduation.

In the Philippines, UPGI works with key government stakeholders, particularly the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev), Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), to explore and advance opportunities for institutionalizing Graduation principles within national policies, programs, budgets, and delivery mechanisms.

1. Background and Strategic Context

The Philippine government has established policy and institutional mechanisms to reduce poverty, strengthen social protection, and improve access to sustainable livelihood and employment opportunities.

These include the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028, and its 2025 Midterm Update, the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps), the 4Ps National AdvisoryCouncil (NAC), and the Program Convergence Budgeting (PCB) for Livelihood and Employment.

Recent government initiatives have also strengthened the policy framework for supporting households transitioning out of 4Ps, including the Pugay-Tagumpay Graduation Strategy and interagency convergence arrangements.

These developments provide potential opportunities for UPGI to contribute evidence and technical expertise to ongoing government-led efforts.

DEPDEv, as the government’s primary economic policy, planning, coordinating, and monitoring agency, plays an important role in aligning poverty reduction and economic inclusion priorities with national development planning, public investment programming, policy coordination, and monitoring frameworks.

At the same time, operational responsibilities for social protection, livelihood, employment, and 4Ps convergence reside across multiple agencies, particularly DSWD and DOLE.

For UPGI, the strategic opportunity is therefore not simply to promote recognition of the Graduation Approach, but to identify how its distinctive technical expertise can strengthen existing government frameworks, address implementation gaps, and contribute to more effective and sustainable poverty reduction outcomes.

As part of its Program Investment planning, UPGI seeks to identify focused, feasible, and government-owned opportunities where its technical and financial resources could make a catalytic contribution.

This requires a clearer understanding of DEPDev’s priorities, the institutional and policy processes through which Graduation-related support could be advanced, and the specific contribution UPGI could provide.

UPGI is therefore commissioning a rapid strategic scoping exercise to inform its partnership and investment decisions, including the potential need for an embedded technical resource within DEPDev.

For the purpose of this assignment, BRAC’s Graduation approach refers to an integrated, sequenced, and context-adapted approach that combines social protection, livelihood and economic inclusion support, coaching or mentoring, financial inclusion, and other services to build sustainable pathways out of extreme poverty. The consultant should distinguish this approach from existing government definitions and processes relating to 4Ps program graduation while identifying areas of alignment and complementarity.

2. Purpose of the Assignment

The primary purpose of this consultancy is to identify, assess, and prioritize strategic opportunities for BRAC UPGI to support DEPDev and relevant government partners in advancing the integration and operationalization of Graduation principles within Philippine poverty reduction, social protection, and economic inclusion systems.

The assignment is intended to inform UPGI’s program investment decisions by determining where its technical assistance and resources could generate the greatest strategic value, strengthen government ownership, and contribute to sustainable institutionalization and potential scale.

The consultancy should also assess whether an embedded UPGI-supported technical resource within DEPDev is an appropriate and effective modality for advancing identified priorities.

The assignment should result in practical recommendations rather than a broad institutional assessment or an open-ended mapping of potential partnerships.

3. Specific Objectives

The consultant will:

Objective 1: Identify strategic policy and institutional entry points

Assess DEPDev’s current and emerging priorities and identify specific policy, planning, investment programming, and coordination processes through which Graduation principles could be meaningfully advanced.

Objective 2: Assess alignment with existing government initiatives

Examine the alignment between BRAC’s Graduation approach and relevant Philippine government frameworks, particularly the PDP (specifically, the sections on economic inclusion, livelihoods, and poverty reduction), 4Ps, 4Ps NAC, PCB for Livelihood and Employment, and other social protection policies and programs..

Identify existing strengths, implementation gaps, and opportunities for UPGI to provide additional technical value without duplicating ongoing government efforts.

Objective 3: Determine government demand and UPGI’s potential contribution

Identify priority areas where relevant government counterparts demonstrate a need for, and interest in, UPGI’s expertise. Assess the institutional feasibility, political and policy environment, and potential for government leadership and ownership.

Objective 4: Prioritize investment and engagement opportunities

Develop a small set of practical support options and assess their strategic relevance, feasibility, resource implications, sustainability, and potential contribution to the institutionalization and scaling of Graduation-informed approaches.

Objective 5: Recommend an actionable engagement and resourcing arrangement

Recommend the most appropriate next steps and technical assistance modality for UPGI, including whether an embedded technical resource within DEPDev is justified. Where appropriate, develop a proposed position TOR and indicative 12-month work plan.

4. Scope of Work and Primary Responsibilities

The consultant will undertake the following activities:

Task 1: Inception and Targeted Policy and Institutional Review

Conduct a focused review of relevant government and UPGI documents to develop an initial understanding of the policy environment, government priorities, and potential entry points. Documents may include:

  1. The current PDP and relevant implementation and monitoring documents.

  2. DEPDev’s relevant policy priorities (Social Protection) and poverty reduction strategies.

  3. 4Ps programme documents and related economic inclusion initiatives.

  4. Available 4Ps NAC documents, including its mandate, membership, and relevant meeting or policy materials.

  5. PCB for Livelihood and Employment, including relevant DOLE coordination and budgeting processes

  6. Relevant Graduation evidence, evaluations, and UPGI strategy documents.

The document review should focus on identifying practical policy and institutional opportunities, not producing an exhaustive literature review.

The consultant will prepare a brief inception note outlining the proposed approach, priority questions, initial hypotheses, stakeholder consultations, and expected outputs.

Task 2: Conduct Strategic Stakeholder Consultations

Conduct approximately 6–8 key informant interviews and 2–3 small working meetings, subject to stakeholder availability and agreement with UPGI. Priority stakeholders should include appropriate representatives from:

  1. DEPDev officials and technical staff involved in national development planning, poverty reduction, social protection, public investment, and interagency coordination.

  2. Relevant 4Ps and Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) representatives.

  3. Selected 4Ps NAC representatives or member agencies.

  4. Relevant DOLE counterparts involved in livelihood and employment convergence and the associated PCB mechanism, in the Social Protection Floor, and in programs and policies related to child labor and informal workers.

  5. Other relevant government counterparts, where necessary to clarify specific policy or institutional issues.

Interviews and meetings will explore:

  1. What are DEPDev’s and relevant partner agencies’ current priorities concerning poverty reduction, social protection, and economic inclusion?

  2. Potential opportunities to integrate Graduation into the PDP and its implementation mechanisms.

  3. Possible complementarities between Graduation and 4Ps.

  4. Opportunities to advance Graduation-related policy dialogue or coordination through the 4Ps NAC.

  5. Institutional needs, constraints, decision-making processes, and potential policy windows.

  6. The type of technical assistance that would be most useful from UPGI.

  7. Potential functions, placement, and priorities of an embedded UPGI-supported staff member.

Meetings should be targeted and discussion-oriented, with no requirement for large-scale workshops or formal multi-stakeholder events. Existing meetings may be used where appropriate.

Task 3: Analysis and Prioritization of Support Opportunities

Synthesize findings from the document review, interviews, and working meetings to identify and prioritize potential areas for UPGI support. The consultant will distinguish between immediate actions, medium-term technical support, and longer-term opportunities requiring additional government decisions.

Task 4: Develop the Embedded Staff TOR and 12-Month Work Plan

Based on the scoping findings, assess the most suitable mechanism through which UPGI could provide support. Options may include:

  • An embedded UPGI-supported technical resource within DEPDev.

  • Time-bound technical assistance or technical specialist.

  • Targeted policy, research, o technical advisory support

  • A phased combination of these approaches.

The assessment should consider the advantages, limitations, expected costs, institutional requirements, and sustainability implications of each option.

If embedding is recommended, the consultant will prepare a proposed TOR specifying:

  • Position purpose an expected contribution to government priorities.

  • Key responsibilities and expected deliverables.

  • Required qualifications and competencies

  • Performance measures and review arrangements

  • Indicative duration and support requirements

The consultant should also prepare an indicative 12-month work plan with quarterly milestones, outputs, responsible counterparts, and review points.

Task 5. Develop a Strategic Investment Recommendation for UPGI

Prepare a concise recommendation for UPGI identifying the preferred area or areas of engagement. The recommendation should clearly explain:

  • What UPGI should prioritize: One or two most promising opportunities for strategic support

  • Why these are priorities: Evidence of government demand and strategic relevance.

  • What UPGI should invest: Indicative staffing, technical assistance, coordination, and other support requirements, with cost assumptions and gaps identified.

  • What results could be expected: realistic 12-month outputs and institutional milestones, and their potential contribution to longer-term scale.

The work plan should translate the proposed responsibilities into a sequenced set of activities, deliverables, milestones, and timelines. It should identify relevant counterparts, dependencies, and areas requiring additional technical support from UPGI.

Task 6: Validation and Finalization

Present the findings and draft deliverables to UPGI and designated government counterparts through a small validation meeting or focused discussions. Incorporate feedback and finalize the scoping report, proposed embedded staff TOR, and 12-month work plan.

5. Methodology

The assignment will use a rapid, qualitative, and consultative approach comprising:

  1. Document review: Focused review of relevant policy, programme, and institutional documents.

  2. Key informant interviews: Semi-structured interviews with selected government stakeholders.

  3. Small working meetings: Targeted discussions to clarify priorities, test emerging findings, and identify feasible support options.

  4. Synthesis and co-design: Analysis of findings and preparation of the proposed embedded staff TOR and work plan.

  5. Validation: Focused review with UPGI and designated DEPDev counterparts.

The consultant will coordinate with UPGI to agree on the final interview list, documents to be reviewed, and arrangements for meetings. UPGI will facilitate introductions where appropriate.

6. Expected Deliverables and Timeline

Deliverable 1: Inception Note and Scoping Framework (Week 1)

An inception note outlining the proposed methodology, initial hypotheses, interview guide, document review plan, and proposed list of stakeholders to be consulted.

Deliverable 2: Scoping Findings and Prioritized Support Options (Week 3)

A concise synthesis of findings from the document review, stakeholder interviews, and consultations. The findings should identify potential entry points through the PDP, 4Ps, and 4Ps NAC, highlight institutional constraints, and recommend prioritized areas for UPGI support.

Deliverable 3: Proposed Engagement Arrangement and 12-Month Work Plan (Week 3)

A proposed technical assistance arrangement outlining the recommended engagement modality, including a draft Terms of Reference for embedded staff where justified. The deliverable should also include a 12-month work plan detailing key milestones, expected outputs, institutional counterparts, and dependencies.

Deliverable 4: Final Scoping Report and Validation Discussion (Week 4)

A consolidated final scoping report incorporating findings, prioritized recommendations, a finalized draft TOR and 12-month work plan, and proposed next steps for UPGI and DEPDev. The consultant will also facilitate a validation discussion with relevant stakeholders.

Final outputs should be:

  • Evidence-informed and grounded in Philippine government context

  • Strategically focused rather than prescriptive

  • Explicit regarding UPGI’s additionality and potential value for money

  • Realistic about what can be achieved with a 12-month engagement

  • Useful for UPGI’s management decisions and subsequent discussions with government counterparts

7. Level of Effort

The assignment will require a maximum of 15 working days of consultant LOE, spread over approximately 3 months, depending on stakeholder availability. Adjustments may be agreed with UPGI within the maximum level of effort.

8. Coordination and Reporting

The consultant will report directly to the Programme Director, who will provide strategic guidance, review key deliverables, and coordinate internal feedback.

The consultant will maintain regular communication with UPGI, particularly at inception, following the initial consultations, and before finalizing the recommended investment options.

The consultant will not make commitments on behalf of UPGI regarding technical assistance, financing, staff deployment, or formal government partnerships.

9. Required Skills and Qualifications

The Consultant should possess:
